items.fact: The Tweez 300 GUI's camera is the Kinetix with serial A23H723003: its main form (window class TArTw300GUIClientMainForm) is titled 'Tweez 300 GUI  - Kinetix A23H723003-PVCAM - RELEASED.' The serial is read off the tweezers software itself, which is the reading the store's tweez300_software_opens_the_red_arm_camera entry names as the one that settles it. Under camera_bodies_are_told_apart_by_serial (A23H723003 is the blue arm), the GUI holds the blue-arm body, not the red one, unless the bodies have changed arms since 2026-09-03.

items.fact: A process having pvcam64.dll loaded does not mean it holds a camera: at 13:10 and 13:28 the Tweez 300 GUI still had pvcam64.dll (and earlier pvcamDDI.dll) loaded while its camera was released and Micro-Manager opened both Kinetix bodies. A detector that reads loaded modules can therefore refuse but never permit; the GUI's main-form title (' - RELEASED.' suffix) distinguishes the two states.

items.fact: The Tweez 300 GUI releases and re-takes its camera only through the 'Release Camera' / 'Grab Camera' item of the right-click menu on the GUI root item of its tree. There is no TCP, COM or Python route. REA's tweez_control.py (camera status|release|grab) drives that menu item by UI automation, moving the real mouse, and reads the state back from the window title. The GUI refuses the release while a calibration is active, a view is recording, or a ROI is active, and refuses camera operations while released ('Camera released - can't perform this operation!'). Verified live by REA on 2026-10-13 (three release/grab cycles).

items.fact: REA reaches the LUN-F by two routes. (1) nis_laser: a server running inside NIS-Elements (started by the macro start_server.mac), reached over TCP 127.0.0.1:5995, calling NIS's MultiLaser functions; it needs NIS running, reads lasers, levels, shutters and light path, and gates every light-adding write on a limits file and the light-path position read at that moment. Its log holds 248 commands from 2026-10-23 to 2026-10-30, the last an all_off. (2) lunf_direct: with NIS closed, power as an SPI word to a 12-bit quad DAC behind FTDI interface 'FT4222 A' (0-5 V full scale) and on/off as NI-DAQ digital lines Dev1/port0/line2, 4, 6, 8 (405, 488, 561, 640 nm; active high). REA's FINDINGS.md records all four lines lit and dark on command, NIS closed, on 2026-10-13, with the person watching; whether a cold boot without NIS needs NIS's GPIO start-up sequence replayed is open.

items.fact: With NIS-Elements closed (nis_ar.exe not running), FTDI enumeration lists the LUN-F's FT4222 board as four interfaces 'FT4222 A' to 'FT4222 D', serials 00294-BOA to 00294-BOD, LocIds 5921 to 5924, each with Flags 2 (high-speed, not opened by any process); LocId 5921 matches the chip location NIS's device database gives for the LUN-F. NI-DAQmx lists one device, Dev1, a PCIe-6323, with port0 lines 2, 4, 6 and 8 present. The NIS laser server was not reachable (connection refused on 127.0.0.1:5995), as expected with NIS closed.
items.how: Read-only driver enumeration at 13:28 -0800: FT_CreateDeviceInfoList and FT_GetDeviceInfoList (ftd2xx), DAQmxGetSysDevNames, DAQmxGetDevProductType, DAQmxGetDevSerialNum and DAQmxGetDevDOLines (nicaiu). No device was opened, no SPI word, GPIO or digital line was written, no light. The refused server connection is in the hwcheck reports.
items.note: This is the 'device flag' detector kind of plan.md 4.6.10 working passively: FT_FLAGS_OPENED (bit 0) reports a holder without opening the device. What the flag reads while NIS runs was not measured today. Four other FTDI nodes read Flags 1 with empty description and serial (opened by some process); which programs hold them was not established.
